question: Does installing MATLAB still install Java?
answer:
Based on MATLAB R2026b [4][5]: no, starting in R2026b MATLAB no longer includes Java as part of its installation; before R2026b, Windows and Linux installations did include Java Runtime [4][5].

After installing MATLAB, you can install the MATLAB Support for OpenJDK add-on or any compatible OpenJDK distribution, and MATLAB continues to support OpenJDK on all platforms [5]. With the add-on, you install it from Add-Ons in the Home tab's Environment section, then run `jenv -clear` in the Command Window so MATLAB uses it [4]. R2026b also supports OpenJDK 25 from adoptium.net [5].

The same applies to deployment: MATLAB Runtime no longer includes the JRE in R2026b, so deployed apps that use Java must be configured with the `matlab_jenv` command to use an external JRE or JDK [1].

studyNotes.focus: Whether a standard MATLAB installation still bundles Java, or whether Java must now be installed separately.

keyPoints.text: Starting in R2026b, MATLAB no longer includes Java as part of its installation on Windows and Linux.
Users can install the MATLAB Support for OpenJDK add-on or any compatible OpenJDK distribution after installing MATLAB, and MATLAB continues to support OpenJDK on all platforms.
MATLAB Runtime no longer includes the JRE starting in R2026b, so deployed apps using Java must have a supported Java configured with matlab_jenv.
Before R2026b, MATLAB installations on Windows and Linux included Java Runtime.

conflicts.text: Source 4 describes Oracle Java being bundled in releases before R2026b and that Java will be removed in a future release, while sources 4 and 5 state that R2026b no longer includes Java; these are consistent on timing but source 4's wording is a pre-release forward-looking note.

mayBeStale.text: Source 4 is a release-notes excerpt that still contains 'behavior change in future release' wording about Oracle Java, which is superseded by the R2026b statement that Java is no longer installed.
Install and configuration steps (add-on names, jenv and matlab_jenv usage) are specific to R2026b and may change in later releases.
